first-couple-ocean-steady.label: First-time couple, wants the ocean, sensitive stomach

recommendations.hook: Mid-deck oceanview: steady sleep, morning light
recommendations.reason: Cabin 5180 sits midship on a lower deck where motion is minimal—that helps with the queasiness one of you experiences. The oceanview means you both wake to the real ocean, and you're low enough on the ship that the motion stays gentle. It's on Deck 5, so you're not fighting crowds to get topside.

recommendations.hook: Ocean view cabin, center of ship, settled nights
recommendations.reason: Just a few doors from 5180, this cabin offers the same oceanview and midship steadiness. Since these two are nearly identical, the tie-breaker is that 5182 sits slightly further aft within the midship zone, which some travelers find fractionally calmer. Either would serve you well; pick based on availability.

recommendations.hook: Balcony higher up: ocean view with private air
recommendations.reason: A mid-deck balcony cabin on Deck 9 gives you that ocean view and a little private outdoor space to yourself. You'll feel the motion a touch more up here than on Deck 5, but the balcony means you can step outside for fresh air when the ship rocks, and it's often easier to manage queasiness with a bit of real breeze. The trade-off is higher-deck exposure for your own piece of outdoors.

recommendations.hook: Balcony cabin, midship perch for sleeping light sleepers
recommendations.reason: Deck 12 is higher and steadier than the very top decks, and this midship balcony keeps you away from the forward and aft areas where you'd hear more machinery and activity. Light sleepers often do better midship and away from high-traffic zones. The balcony lets you wake to ocean without the noise exposure of the main hallways.

recommendations.hook: Mid-deck midship balcony: quiet, stable, oceanfront
recommendations.reason: Deck 10 is still in the sweet spot for motion—not as low as Deck 5, but steadier than the upper decks—and midship placement helps both light sleepers and anyone dealing with queasiness. The balcony gives you ocean views and a private retreat from hallway noise. It's a solid all-rounder for your needs.

steerClear.reason: Deck 13 forward is high and far from the center, where motion and noise from early-morning deck activity are both more pronounced. With one of you light-sleeping and the other queasy, you want the steadiest, quietest spot—not the top end of the ship.
This oceanview sits aft on Deck 5. Although it's low, aft cabins tend to move more and can pick up noise from the stern and crew areas, which works against your light-sleep and queasiness concerns.

Deck 17 is the highest and most exposed to motion. The ocean view is lovely, but the upper-deck pitch and roll will aggravate queasiness, and the isolation from the center of the ship can amplify noise from the deck above and activity nearby.

couple-ocean-balcony-treat.label: Couple treating themselves to a great balcony

recommendations.hook: Balcony where the ocean fills your whole view, midship peace
recommendations.reason: 9190 sits midship on a high deck where you get an unobstructed ocean balcony and the quiet you're after. Being in the middle of the ship keeps you away from elevator banks and the forward anchor noise that plagues couples looking for real peace. This is the kind of room where two people can hear each other on the balcony.

recommendations.hook: Balcony on deck 10, midship calm without the crowds
recommendations.reason: Deck 10 midship gives you the full balcony experience without being sandwiched between pool decks and late-night venues. You'll catch the ocean view from a quieter vantage, and the midship position protects you from the bow's rougher water and stern's nightlife bleed-through. Good ocean sightlines, real solitude.

recommendations.hook: High-deck balcony in the peaceful heart of the ship
recommendations.reason: Deck 11 midship offers the elevation you want with an ocean balcony and no foot traffic above or below you on this quiet stretch. You're treating yourselves, and this room delivers that feeling—high enough to see the horizon without the premium price tag of suites. The midship location means minimal throb from engines.

recommendations.hook: Balcony on deck 12, midship quiet in an elevated spot
recommendations.reason: Deck 12 is one of the higher open decks, and midship keeps you centered away from noise. This balcony gives you real ocean views and a sense of separation from the ship's busier zones. It's the kind of room where a couple can sit outside and breathe.

recommendations.hook: Midship ocean balcony—quiet and intimate for two
recommendations.reason: Deck 10 midship, unobstructed ocean view, positioned where the ship's motion and ambient noise are lowest. You get the balcony you wanted and the peace you asked for in one room. Not the highest deck, but solid sightlines and genuine quiet.

steerClear.reason: Forward on deck 9 means closer to anchor equipment and daytime bow activity, which disrupts the quiet retreat you're looking for. Forward cabins also catch early morning traffic from crew and early risers heading to breakfast.

This is a Haven suite, not a balcony cabin—it comes with suite amenities and perks you didn't ask for, and the price reflects that. You wanted a nice ocean-view balcony, not the full resort experience, so you'd be overpaying for extras.
Deck 5 is low and forward, meaning more engine vibration, more bow wash visible (and heard), and exposure to staff corridors. You'd feel the ship work more than relax on your own balcony.

recommendations.hook: The Haven suite with midship ocean views and private perks
recommendations.reason: This is a The Haven suite—Norwegian's top-tier private complex with its own lounge, restaurant, butler service, and exclusive sundeck. You get the real suite experience with a genuine ocean balcony, plus all the extras that come with the Haven keycard access. For an anniversary celebrating without budget limits, this is the gold standard on the ship.

recommendations.hook: Haven luxury with a second suite option to consider first
recommendations.reason: Another The Haven suite, also midship with ocean views and full suite privileges. It's essentially identical to 13228—same complex, same butler service, same exclusivity. The honest tie-breaker: 13228 sits a little further forward, which some travelers prefer for the feel of the ship, but either is genuinely excellent.

recommendations.hook: Haven suite on a higher deck for unobstructed views and light
recommendations.reason: This The Haven cabin is on Deck 14, giving you more elevation and unobstructed sightlines—no cabins in front of you blocking the horizon. You still get all the Haven perks: private lounge, restaurant, concierge. Higher decks mean more sky and a cleaner view of the ocean, which makes the balcony experience feel more expansive.

recommendations.hook: Haven suite aft with afternoon sun and exclusive amenities
recommendations.reason: A The Haven suite positioned aft on Deck 14, which means afternoon and evening light hits your balcony later in the day. You still have full access to the Haven's private restaurant, lounge, and concierge—all the suite perks. The aft position is quieter and more secluded than forward, perfect for an anniversary couple wanting privacy.

recommendations.hook: Haven suite with starboard light and a sense of quiet escape
recommendations.reason: Another The Haven cabin, midship on the starboard side, with the full suite experience. You're getting dedicated butler service, the private Haven restaurant, and access to a reserved sundeck—genuine luxury perks that justify the celebration price. The starboard side catches afternoon light and feels notably more removed from the main passenger flow.

steerClear.reason: This is a Balcony cabin, not a suite—no butler service, no exclusive lounge, no private restaurant. For a no-budget-ceiling anniversary, you'd be missing the real suite perks you want.

This is a Balcony cabin on Deck 12 with no cabins below it (that's public space). You'll get noise and chair scraping from the areas directly above you in the early mornings—not the peaceful anniversary experience you're after.

recommendations.hook: Balcony steps from shows, pools, and constant action
recommendations.reason: Cabin 9184 is a midship balcony on Deck 9, putting you dead center on the ship where the main entertainment venues and pools cluster around you. Your kids can dart between the action without getting lost, and you'll catch the energy even from your own space. Close enough to find the fun, far enough to retreat when bedtime hits.

recommendations.hook: Mid-deck balcony lets four of you sprawl in comfort
recommendations.reason: This is another midship balcony, Deck 10, with the same location perks as 9184—near the heart of the ship's activities. Deck 10 is a step up from 9, so you're still central but slightly further from the chaos if the kids get overstimulated by day. Two separate sleeping areas help when little ones need quiet and you need to stay engaged.

recommendations.hook: Balcony action-adjacent without the overhead noise problem
recommendations.reason: Midship Deck 10 balcony, same convenience as the previous two, but 10180 avoids the cabins directly below public decks that tend to get early-morning foot traffic and chair scraping. You're still in the thick of things, just without that overhead disruption—solid for families who want access to the buzz without the background soundtrack.

recommendations.hook: Forward balcony keeps you near dining and early activity
recommendations.reason: Deck 12, forward position: you're placed between the main restaurants and the forward pools, so mornings and mealtimes flow naturally. Forward cabins on this ship wake early because that's where foot traffic starts, which works for a family keen to hit the buffet and activities first. Your kids will see the action ramping up before anyone sleeping midship.

recommendations.hook: Midship balcony on top decks, farthest from engine noise
recommendations.reason: Balcony on Deck 13, midship: you gain the location advantage of being central but on a higher deck where the roar and vibration from the engines below fade significantly. Good for families who want the hub without the mechanical hum that lower decks sometimes pick up. Still steps away from the action, just quieter underfoot.

recommendations.hook: Midship balcony with good sightlines to the main stage
recommendations.reason: Deck 9 midship balcony positioned near the main entertainment venues. You can keep tabs on what's happening without leaving your balcony, and the location is central enough that kids can find their way back to you easily between activities. Slightly less prime than 9184 only because it's a touch further aft within the midship zone, but the tradeoff is negligible.

steerClear.reason: Deck 5 forward position is far from the action you want—you'll be spending the whole cruise walking back from activities instead of being in the thick of it. Lower decks also pick up more engine vibration and water noise, which works against your family-friendly vibe.
Deck 13 forward—too quiet and removed from the main pools and shows where families congregate. You wanted to be near all the action, and forward on a top deck puts you on the wrong end of the ship.

Deck 15 midship, but this cabin sits directly above public space (no cabins above it), which means daytime foot traffic, deck chairs scraping, and activity noise directly overhead throughout your stay. For a family that doesn't mind noise, it's still an unnecessary distraction.

family-value-space.label: Budget family that needs room

recommendations.hook: Oceanview cabin, midship, four of you, real budget sense
recommendations.reason: This oceanview sits midship on Deck 5, giving your family a real ocean view without the premium price of higher decks. You've got enough room for four without blowing your lean budget, and the location keeps noise down — no early-morning foot traffic from the forward end or bar spillover from aft. That's the sweet spot for families watching their money.

recommendations.hook: Ocean porthole, midship steady, four in one real cabin
recommendations.reason: Right next to 5182 and identical — midship oceanview on Deck 5. The only reason this ranks second is coin toss; both are equally solid for your crew. If 5182 is booked, grab this one without hesitation.

recommendations.hook: Oceanview midship, tight budget, family of four sleeps well
recommendations.reason: Also midship oceanview on Deck 5, just a couple doors down. Same logic as the first two — solid space, real ocean, no premium for a balcony you didn't ask for. Three excellent options on this stretch; any of the three will do your family right.

recommendations.hook: Oceanview cabin, midship, four bunks without the markup
recommendations.reason: Still on Deck 5 midship, oceanview, and honestly just as good as the top three. You're starting to see the pattern — this deck and location deliver what you need at the price you want. Rank 4 mainly because the first three came up first; there's no flaw here.

recommendations.hook: Oceanview balcony, family fit, higher deck, lean price holds
recommendations.reason: Deck 12 balcony that doesn't charge balcony premiums the way higher categories do. Your four will fit, you get the ocean, and you're still steering clear of the suites and premium cabins that would blow your budget. It's higher up (which some families like for the view), and the price stays lean.

steerClear.reason: This is The Haven — Norwegian's suite complex with butler service and private lounges. The nightly cost per cabin will wreck your lean budget fast, and you didn't ask for those extras.
Studio cabin on Deck 12 — these are built and priced for solo travelers, not families of four. You'll find yourself cramped and the price-per-person won't work in your favor.

Forward oceanview on Deck 5. While it's an oceanview and affordable, the forward end means more foot traffic, activity noise from the bow, and early-morning rustling when the ship is in port. For a family watching budget, the quieter midship cabins (5178–5190) are genuinely better.

quiet-retirees-calm.label: Quiet-seeking retirees

recommendations.hook: Oceanview on Deck 5, midship calm and quiet
recommendations.reason: Cabin 5180 sits in the dead center of the ship on a lower deck, surrounded by other cabins that buffer you from elevator noise and foot traffic. You get a real ocean view to settle into during those early mornings when you want silence, and nothing above or below you is a public space that'll bring scraping chairs at dawn. This is the textbook choice for a couple who want to wake up rested.

recommendations.hook: Quiet oceanview, midship with neighbors all around
recommendations.reason: Nearly identical to 5180 in every way that matters to you—same peaceful midship spot, same low deck, same real ocean view—so the tie-breaker is pure cabin luck. If 5180 books, this one delivers the same promise. Two older travelers who sleep lightly will both rest well here.

recommendations.hook: Ocean view in the ship's middle, zero noise above
recommendations.reason: You've got cabins on all sides of you and no public areas directly overhead, which means no chairs scraping or early-morning events to jar you awake. The oceanview gives you that calm sight line you want, and being midship on Deck 5 keeps things as settled as the Aura gets. A solid third option if the first two slip away.

recommendations.hook: Midship balcony cabin, surrounded by sleeping neighbors
recommendations.reason: This one trades the oceanview window for a private balcony, but it keeps the same midship quiet that matters most. You can step out for fresh air at sunrise without leaving your own space, and being completely surrounded by other cabins means nobody's dragging deck chairs at odd hours above or beside you.

recommendations.hook: Higher deck balcony, quiet midship perch for peace
recommendations.reason: If you prefer to be higher up and can trade a window for a balcony, Deck 10 midship keeps you in the same calm zone. Still surrounded by other guests, still zero public noise overhead, and a balcony gives you your own private moment without walking far. The higher elevation is a nice bonus for a couple who want calm air on their own terms.

steerClear.reason: Deck 13 forward on the high decks is less steady and pitches more in any sea state. You told us rest is the priority, and the higher you go forward, the more the ship moves—exactly the opposite of what a light-sleeping couple needs.

There are no cabins directly above you—that's public deck space—which means chairs scraping and early-morning setup noise starts right over your head. You'll hear it, and falling back to sleep won't happen easily.

Forward cabins feel more motion and activity the farther forward you go. You're also closer to crew alleys and the forward elevators, so the peace you're after gets crowded by foot traffic earlier in the day.

value-hunter-ocean.label: Value hunter who still wants the sea

recommendations.hook: Oceanview on a lower deck—budget stretches, view stays
recommendations.reason: Cabin 5180 is an oceanview on Deck 5, one of the lower passenger decks, which means real savings compared to higher-up balconies without sacrificing your ocean view. You get that water view you wanted while keeping costs down—the smart money move when you're watching budget and refusing to pick an inside cabin.

recommendations.hook: Balcony midship where the budget meets the ocean
recommendations.reason: This midship balcony on Deck 9 sits in the dead center of the ship, so you're paying less per night than forward or aft cabins at this level while keeping the private outdoor space. The tradeoff is clear: you give up premium position, you keep your view and your wallet.

recommendations.hook: Ocean view, midship stability, lower-deck pricing
recommendations.reason: Deck 5 oceanview positioned midship offers steadier motion than forward or aft, and the price reflects it—lower than comparable cabins higher up the ship. If any light chop bothers you, this position helps; if not, you're just pocketing the savings.

recommendations.hook: Balcony on Deck 12—height without the premium sticker
recommendations.reason: A balcony this high up on the ship usually commands top dollar, but 12102 on the forward port side is priced lower than you'd expect because of its forward position. You get elevation and that private outdoor space—just not the most coveted spot on deck, which is precisely how you save.

recommendations.hook: Balcony midship, Deck 10—the sweet spot for two
recommendations.reason: Deck 10 midship balcony gives you a genuine ocean view, an outdoor balcony, and midship positioning that keeps the cabin price honest. At this height and position, you're not paying for premium real estate, just solid comfort and the view you wanted.

recommendations.hook: Ocean view, midship Deck 5—where budget and ocean meet
recommendations.reason: Another Deck 5 midship oceanview, 5206 sits in nearly the same spot as 5192 but a couple cabins over—same logic, same value. Either works; pick whichever feels right for your sailing date.

steerClear.reason: Forward balcony on Deck 9 commands premium pricing for the position. You're explicitly watching your budget; spending more for the front-of-ship view contradicts that priority.
This is a Haven suite—priced far beyond what a couple watching budget should pay. The perks (restaurant, lounge, concierge) add cost; you didn't ask for those extras.
Forward oceanview on Deck 5 carries a premium over midship cabins at the same level with no view difference. You're saving money by picking the middle of the ship, not the prow.

solo-first-value.label: Solo first-timer, budget-minded

recommendations.hook: Studio solo cabin, no single supplement hit
recommendations.reason: Studio 12501 is purpose-built for you as a solo traveler and priced to match—no single supplement to eat into your budget. You get your own private stateroom without paying the penalty couples do. Access to the Studio Lounge is a real perk on a solo cruise, a quiet spot to read or meet other travelers if you feel like it.

recommendations.hook: Studio forward deck, same value, slightly different location
recommendations.reason: 12503 is another Studio with no supplement—identical layout and pricing to 12501, just positioned a little further forward on Deck 12. If 12501 books out, this one gives you the same thing: your own space at a solo traveler's rate, plus Studio Lounge access. The choice between them comes down to whether you prefer forward or farther aft; both are equally good value.

recommendations.hook: Mid-deck oceanview, genuine savings over balcony prices
recommendations.reason: 5180 is an oceanview on Deck 5, mid-ship, with no balcony premium tacked on. You still wake to real ocean, which beats an inside cabin, but you're paying less than the balcony crowd. For a budget-conscious solo traveler, this is honest value—you get the view without the deck space you'd have to maintain.

recommendations.hook: Oceanview mid-deck, steady position with light sleeper bonus
recommendations.reason: 5182 sits mid-ship on Deck 5 with an ocean view. Being in the middle of the ship keeps motion minimal, which matters if you're a light sleeper and don't want to feel the sway. You're still paying oceanview rates, not balcony markup, so your budget stays in check while you get the benefit of a quieter, steadier ride.

recommendations.hook: Oceanview, steadiest mid-ship spot on lower deck
recommendations.reason: 5184 is oceanview, mid-deck, mid-ship—the sweet spot for passengers who sleep light and travel light on budget. Lower on the ship means less movement, real ocean views without a balcony surcharge. You're maximizing the dollar-to-comfort ratio: steady, ocean-facing, no frills you don't need.

steerClear.reason: Deck 13 forward is up high and toward the bow, where pitch and sway are most noticeable. For a first-time solo traveler watching costs, a room that moves more than it needs to isn't worth the gamble.

Deck 17 is the top; any wave action is magnified up there. Combined with forward placement, this cabin moves noticeably more than lower, mid-ship options—and it will cost more too. Not a good match for your budget or your first cruise experience.

Forward oceanview on Deck 5 means you're at the bow, where the ship pitches and rises into swells. As a first-time cruiser, you don't know yet how your stomach handles it; a mid-ship cabin gives you more cushion for that learning curve.

recommendations.hook: Studio near the action, your own space to retreat
recommendations.reason: Studio 12501 sits forward on Deck 12, steps from the public spaces and restaurants where your group will gather. You get a room sized and priced for one person with no single supplement — the homework is done for your budget. Access to the Studio Lounge means you can meet up with your group without leaving the deck, then slip back to your own quiet corner when you need breathing room.

recommendations.hook: Studio in the center, close to everything without feeling crowded
recommendations.reason: 12545 is a Studio on Deck 12, positioned center-ship where the main flow of people and activity moves through. You're near the elevators and main corridors, so catching up with your group takes seconds. Like 12501, you have the solo traveler advantage — no supplement, your own lounge — but this one puts you dead center in the action.

recommendations.hook: Balcony on mid-deck, close to pools and shows
recommendations.reason: Balcony 9170 sits mid-ship on Deck 9, near the heart of the ship's social spaces — pools, lounges, and show venues. You're steps from where your group will naturally gather, so you can find them without hunting. The balcony gives you a bonus: a quiet spot of your own to decompress after group time, or to watch the ship move through the water before the evening crowd hits.

recommendations.hook: Mid-deck balcony, close to bars and evening action
recommendations.reason: 9182 is nearly identical to 9170 — both mid-ship balconies on Deck 9 — but 9182 sits slightly closer to the evening entertainment zones and bar areas where your group might gather after dinner. If your group tends toward nighttime hangouts, this gives you a fractionally shorter walk. The tie-breaker is location within the deck; otherwise they trade places.

recommendations.hook: Oceanview on mid-deck, near the group, money left over
recommendations.reason: 5180 is an Oceanview on Deck 5, positioned mid-ship where you stay close to shared spaces. It costs less than a balcony, so your budget stretches further — money you can spend on group dinners or excursions. You still have a real ocean view, which beats being cooped up inside, and you're in the thick of activity without the premium balcony price tag.

steerClear.reason: Deck 17 is the top of the ship — far from the main action and dining areas your group will use. You'll spend half your time hunting for them on the elevators, defeating the whole point of staying near the group.

This aft oceanview on Deck 5 sits at the back of the ship, away from the restaurants, pools, and public hangouts where a group naturally clusters. You'd be isolated from the action you came to be part of.

big-group-together.label: Group that wants to stay together

recommendations.hook: Midship oceanview where your group stays close together
recommendations.reason: 5190 sits in the middle of the ship on deck 5, which keeps your whole party within shouting distance of everything — the dining rooms, the main theaters, the bars. You'll have an ocean view without paying for a balcony, and you're positioned to drift to any deck or activity without a long trek. For a group that wants to be near each other and near everything, this is your anchor point.

recommendations.hook: Oceanview steps from the action, same deck as your crew
recommendations.reason: Right next door to 5190, 5192 gives you the same midship convenience and real ocean light. Book these two together and half your group is already plotted — close enough to meet for dinner without coordinating across the ship, far enough that nobody's stuck in someone else's cabin all day.

recommendations.hook: Third oceanview cabin keeps the cluster tight
recommendations.reason: Still midship on deck 5, this one puts three of you on the same stretch of corridor. You're all deck-5 neighbors with sight lines to the same activities and restaurants. For a group traveling together, being on the same deck with ocean cabins means everyone sees the same sunrise and you're not splitting time between different floors.

recommendations.hook: Oceanview on the block — group just gets bigger
recommendations.reason: 5194 is the fourth oceanview cabin in this midship pocket on deck 5. At this point you're booking as a cluster. Stay on the same deck, same corridor, real ocean views, and you're steps from the elevators that serve every major public space on the ship.

recommendations.hook: Balcony cabin upgrades the view, keeps you midship
recommendations.reason: If your budget stretches, 9190 is a balcony on deck 9 in the middle of the ship — you get that outdoor space plus the same proximity to everything that makes midship work. You're not far from your deck-5 crew (elevators are close), and a balcony cabin in a group gives one couple a little extra without splitting the group across the ship.

recommendations.hook: Balcony on deck 10 midship — another upgrade option
recommendations.reason: Another midship balcony option if you want to stagger a few people up a deck or two. The midship location keeps travel to common areas tight, and balconies on higher decks feel like a nice step up without the isolation of going full-forward or full-aft.

steerClear.reason: Deck 13 forward puts you far from the heart of the ship — you're a long walk or elevator ride from the main dining and entertainment areas. For a group prioritizing being near each other and near everything, a forward balcony on a high deck pulls you away from the cluster.

This oceanview is in the forward section of deck 5, which means longer walks to reach common spaces from your cabin and harder to meet up quickly. Your group will scatter just trying to get to dinner.

experienced-ocean-midship.label: Experienced cruisers, know they want a real ocean balcony

recommendations.hook: Mid-ship balcony where the ocean meets your private door
recommendations.reason: Cabin 9190 sits dead center on Deck 9, giving you a real ocean balcony with an unobstructed view. You get what you're after—a genuine sea-facing perch, no gimmicks, positioned where the ship's motion settles lowest and steadiest. This is the straightforward balcony cabin you described.

recommendations.hook: Ocean balcony, mid-deck stability, room to breathe
recommendations.reason: Nearly identical to 9190, also mid-ship on Deck 9 with full ocean access and no obstruction. The tie-breaker: 9190 sits a touch deeper into the heart of the ship. Both deliver exactly what you want; pick this if 9190 books out.

recommendations.hook: Steady mid-ship balcony on the higher deck
recommendations.reason: Deck 10 sits higher, so the view stretches further. Mid-ship placement keeps the motion minimal and balanced. You're trading the slightly lower deck position of 9190 for better sightlines and the same steadiness—a real ocean balcony without compromise.

recommendations.hook: Ocean-view balcony, lower deck, proven stability
recommendations.reason: Deck 5 is one of the lowest passenger decks, which means genuinely steady positioning even for someone who's sensitive to any roll. Full ocean view, mid-ship, no obstruction. You lose the height of upper decks but gain the certainty of minimal motion—a fair trade if steadiness is your priority.

recommendations.hook: Mid-deck balcony with clean ocean view
recommendations.reason: Deck 12 balcony, mid-ship placement, unobstructed ocean. You're going higher for a wider perspective and still maintaining the mid-ship stability you're after. Slightly more elevated than Deck 9 options but the same core balance.

steerClear.reason: This is a Haven suite, not a standard balcony cabin. You said no gimmicks and you know what you want—a real ocean balcony. Haven rooms come with butler service and perks you didn't ask for, which drives the price up without delivering what you're after.
Deck 17 sits very high, which means more pronounced motion in any swell. You wanted steady mid-ship balance; going to the top deck works against that comfort.

recommendations.hook: Oceanview on a low, steady deck—your best bet for calm
recommendations.reason: Deck 5 sits low on the ship, which minimizes motion when the ocean gets rough. You get a real ocean view without paying for a balcony upgrade, and the midship position (where the ship flexes least) gives you the steadiest ride on the Aura. For a couple worried about seasickness, this is your foundation.

recommendations.hook: Real ocean view, dead center, rock-solid motion control
recommendations.reason: Same deck and steadiness as 5180, but midship placement is the secret weapon for seasickness—the ship pitches and rolls less here than anywhere else. You still get a window on the water, which helps psychologically when you're feeling queasy, without the balcony premium or the higher-deck motion.

recommendations.hook: Balcony on a stable low deck when you're ready to upgrade
recommendations.reason: If your budget stretches to a balcony, Deck 12 keeps you low enough that motion stays manageable. The midship position again works in your favor. You get fresh air and your own outdoor space—a real comfort if one of you needs to step outside when the tummy feels uncertain.

recommendations.hook: Oceanview, midship stability, and a real view for the price
recommendations.reason: Another solid Deck 5 option in the middle of the ship. You're trading the aft cabins (which pitch more in heavy seas) for the steadiest part of the vessel, all while keeping an oceanview and a comfortable budget.

steerClear.reason: Deck 13 sits high on the ship, which amplifies motion in rough water—the opposite of what you need. Combined with the forward position, this cabin will exaggerate any swell.
Deck 15 is even higher, and forward cabins on the upper decks pitch noticeably in a seaway. This room would work against your seasickness concern, not with it.
While Deck 5 is steady, the forward position on this deck gets more vertical motion from waves compared to midship. You'd do better a few cabins aft.
